# Worker config (v1)

Schema for `.tera/workers/<name>.hcl` config files. Each decodes to `pkg/config.WorkerBlock` declaring a digital worker — responsibility dispatch, permissions and budgets. The block label is the worker name. A worker declaring the ADR-046 §3.3 `orchestrator` block is REFUSED at load under ADR-136 D5 row 3: the daemon runs no model, so there is no orchestrator agent for it to stand up. So, under ADR-136 D5's worker-embedded agent row, is a worker declaring its own `agent` block, a responsibility `agent` handler, or a non-empty `permissions.agents`. Under ADR-136 D11 a worker still setting `factory`, or declaring an `audit` block, is refused by name too: nothing reads either since the agent runtime went.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `config/workers` |
| Regime | persisted |
| Identity regime | `recipe` — the filename stem is the identity; the file declares exactly one resource, and a block label — where the grammar admits one — must equal the stem (ADR-087 D3) |
| Current version | `v1` |
| Supported versions | `v1` |
| HCL block | `worker` |
| Loader directory | `.tera/workers/<name>.hcl` |
| Go source | `github.com/kottera/kottera/pkg/config.WorkerBlock` |
| Served at | `GET /api/v1/schemas/config/workers/reference` |

## Example

A minimal `workers`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/workers/example-worker.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

worker "example-worker" {
  description = "What this is for, in one line."

  connection "example-connection" {
    value = "env://EXAMPLE_TOKEN"
  }
}
```

| `max_live_environments` | integer | no | `24` | ADR-057 §9 | — | ADR-057 §9 aggregate cap on the live virtual environments this worker's Work Orders hold between them, parked holders included. Unset uses the platform default; -1 removes the cap; 0 is refused, because on this block 0 reads as unlimited for max_concurrent_workorders and as none here, so neither reading is safe — remove the attribute for the default. An edit hot-reloads and changes only the next admission: no live environment is evicted, a cap lowered below the current count refuses new ones until enough end, and a raise re-offers capacity to the Work Orders waiting on it. |
| `safety_poll_interval` | string | no | — | — | — | — |
| `workspace_hold_deadline` | string | no | `24h` | ADR-106 Q2 | — | ADR-106 Q2 hold deadline: how long a Work Order waits for the fleet runner holding its workspace before the workspace is re-provisioned on another runner from source and the session is declared lost. A duration string; 0 holds indefinitely until an operator acts. Not the ADR-106 D11/D12 lease quarantine, which has no timer. |
| `hitl_delegate` | string | no | `none` | ADR-079 D4 | — | ADR-079 D4 delegation policy for this worker's paused Work Orders: none (default) refuses delegate Work Orders outright, assist confines the delegate to its policy allow-list, auto lets it answer whatever it judges answerable. Overridden per type by a work-order type's own hitl_delegate. |
| `activity_partition` | string | no | — | ADR-113 D3 | — | ADR-113 D3's lowest-ranked activity-partition declaration: the partition this worker's dispatches resolve to when neither the work-order type nor the listener declares one. Names a partition an activity_partition recipe declares. Unset is an absence, not a default — a dispatch that resolves to no partition emits, stores and publishes nothing, and there is no fallback partition. A type's own activity_partition overrides this silently, which is why the effective value is recorded on the dispatch. |

## `permissions` block

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `connectors` | string[] | no | — | — | — | — |
| `tools` | string[] | no | — | — | — | The tools this worker may dispatch, each named by a registered capability name or an @group:<name> reference. A system-vault tool answers to two names, its bare stem (screenshot) and its canonical recipe name (system/tools/screenshot), and either may be granted; a user-vault tool is granted by its canonical name. A grant covers exactly the spelling it names: a Work Order type whose capability site names system/tools/screenshot needs that spelling granted, and a bare grant does not cover it, nor the reverse, because on a leaf collision the two spellings are different tools. A tool block declared in kernel HCL has only its bare name. A plugin's tool is granted by its declared address, plugin.<installation>/tools/<stem>, which needs .tera/builds-on/<installation>.hcl in the worker's vault and resolves at load to the release address of the major that file names. The bare stem never grants a plugin's tool, even where the plugin's stem matches it: it grants the system-vault tool of that stem (ADR-156 D7). Writing a release address, plugin.<installation>.v<major>/tools/<stem>, is refused release_address_written, and a declared address into an installation the vault does not build on is refused builds_on_missing. |
| `topics` | string[] | no | — | — | — | — |
| `web_fetch_internal_ranges` | string[] | no | — | ADR-042 §4 (2026-10-07) | — | CIDR ranges this worker's web-fetch may connect to although they are internal destinations (loopback, RFC 1918 and IPv6 unique-local, link-local including 169.254.169.254, multicast, RFC 6598 shared space), which web-fetch otherwise refuses at the dial on every road. Unset or empty admits none. Each entry is a CIDR with no host bits set, IPv4 written in its IPv4 form; an address resolving inside an entry is admitted, and every other internal address is still refused. Read only here: no binding, Work Order step or in_dispatch grant config can open a range, and a call with no worker (the gateway, an interactive call) refuses every internal range. Admitting a range admits every name that resolves into it, through any allow_domains entry the worker's bindings carry. |
| `environments` | block | no | — | — | — | — |

## `capability_credentials` block

Repeatable.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | block label | The capability this block binds credentials and seat pools for, by a name it is registered under, matched exactly. A system-vault tool answers to its bare stem (claude-code) and its canonical name (system/tools/claude-code), and either label binds it. The bare stem binds only that system-vault tool and never a plugin's tool with the same stem (ADR-156 D7), so moving a worker from system/tools/claude-code to a plugin's claude-code means relabelling this block. A plugin's tool is labelled by its declared address, plugin.<installation>/tools/<stem>, which needs .tera/builds-on/<installation>.hcl in the worker's vault and resolves at load to the release address of the major that file names. Writing a release address, plugin.<installation>.v<major>/tools/<stem>, is refused release_address_written, and a declared address into an installation the vault does not build on is refused builds_on_missing. A user-vault tool is labelled by its canonical name, <vault>/tools/<stem>, and a connector by its name. Grant the same spelling in permissions.tools. |
| `seat_pools` | string[] | no | — | — | — | The pools this worker draws a seat from when it dispatches this capability: one seat from each, all-or-nothing (ADR-106 D5). A host pool's members admit the dispatch to a machine and supply no credential, and a pool whose members name a connection supply that connection's credential; a member's connection must be one the tool's toolchains apply, so a pool kept for system/tools/claude-code, whose members name the system vault's connections, cannot be named for a plugin's claude-code, whose toolchains apply the installation's (worker_tool_supply_refused). Give that tool a pool of its own. Declaring both seat_pools and seat_pool is refused. |
| `seat_pool` | string | no | — | — | — | The one-element spelling of seat_pools, retained as an alias: seat_pool = "claude" means seat_pools = ["claude"]. |

## `connection` block

Repeatable.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | block label | The connection this credential is for, by its credential key: a system-vault connection's key is the stem of its .tera/connections/<stem>.hcl recipe, and a plugin installation's is plugin.<installation>/connections/<stem>, which carries no major and needs no builds_on. The key is matched exactly, never as a stem. A key no connection declares is refused at load, naming the worker and the connection, and a plugin key is refused naming the installation when it is not installed or none of its installed majors carries the connection. One block per connection per worker. |
| `value` | string | yes | — | ADR-148 D3 | — | A reference to the worker's credential for the connection, written as a capability_credentials field is and resolved by the same resolver: env://VAR, keychain://service#path, vault://path or secret://<row> - or a literal, which is the credential itself. A reference whose scheme the resolver cannot act on is refused at load. A binding whose reference does not resolve on this daemon is not a load error: it reads as bound but unresolvable to every check that asks whether the worker holds the connection's credential, which is distinct from not bound. |
